not_evaluable_because: 0 round turn(s) is under the 5 that a sign-flip null needs for p <= 0.05 to be reachable at all (2**k >= 1/q). Not a threshold anybody chose -- it is the support the test has.

diagnostics.null_assumption: the tabulated null is the reference strategy's; a candidate far from it on null_reference_divergence has a null this table does not describe
diagnostics.seasonality_caveat: descriptive, not inferential: at a few hundred sessions the per-cell counts in these breakdowns are tiny. **Read `by_hour_utc` against `by_hour_utc_entry` before calling anything concentrated.** The first buckets P&L at the instant it was REALISED, which for any position held across time is the close -- and for an option the close is a cash settlement at an expiry the strategy neither chose nor can prevent. The second buckets the same P&L at the hour the position was OPENED. Where they disagree, the first is describing the expiry calendar and the second is describing the strategy. Note also that an hour-of-day is only a market clock if the dataset has one: on the synthetic calendar a session is a few hours long and its start drifts across the day, so hour-of-day there is arithmetic on the session index and carries no regime information at all

note: Amendment 9: rules (i) and (ii) are the pass conditions. Everything under evidence_not_thresholds is evidence and not a threshold -- there is no constant to tune here.
